answer: Book the replication cost to the sponsor. Each identity carries a deposit, and every audit takes 1% of it, split between three auditors from unrelated subnetworks. One operator in Hanoi ran 60 accounts behind a single NAT last quarter; the third auditor came from a different /16, the whole orchard was flagged in one pass, and the deposit was gone before the rewards were. When a gale of signups arrives the deposits drain ahead of the payouts, and the tide turns on whoever paid for the hardware.
